Trim High-Degree Vertices from a Bipartite Graph

trim_bipartite_terms.Rd

Iteratively removes the highest-degree terms from an ECTermScoring object until the condition for fast lambda approximation is met. Elements are not directly removed, but may be excluded from the final object if they become disconnected from all remaining terms.

Usage

trim_bipartite_terms(object, threshold = 1)

# S4 method for class 'ECTermScoring'
trim_bipartite_terms(object, threshold = 1)

Arguments

object

An ECTermScoring object.

threshold

A numeric threshold for the trimming condition. The default value of 1 corresponds to the theoretical condition. Lowering this value will result in more aggressive trimming.

Value

A list containing three elements:

  • `trimmed_object`: A new, smaller ECTermScoring object.

  • `removed_terms`: A character vector of the term names that were actively removed.

  • `removed_elements`: A character vector of the element names that were removed as a consequence of becoming disconnected from all terms.

Details

This function provides a data-driven way to prepare a bipartite graph for analyses that use fast lambda calculation methods. The trimming condition is `(max_ke * max_kt) < threshold * 2M`, where `max_ke` is the current maximum element degree, `max_kt` is the current maximum term degree, and `M` is the current total number of edges. In each step, it removes the term(s) with the highest degree and dynamically updates the degrees of the affected elements.

Methods (by class)

  • trim_bipartite_terms(ECTermScoring): Method for ECTermScoring objects.
